# Zoho Books standard API-field recognition catalog

> **Closure: complete for every field structure published in the verified 2026-08-31 OpenAPI snapshot, subject to the explicit response-shape omission below.** This is a file-local recognition catalog, not a write-safety contract. Request acceptance and response observation are classified separately; response appearance never implies writability.

## Scope, identity, and reading rules

The sole source is the 42 YAML files in `https://www.zoho.com/books/api/v3/openapi-all.zip`, re-downloaded on 2026-08-31 and verified before extraction as SHA-256 `c6a841bbc81ef882c64b1f2ad4761e350faefba1db7fb36a32daf7112b647559`. Tenant metadata, tenant-defined custom field definitions/values, organization values, UI inference, examples scraped from organizations, and adjacent-product schemas are excluded. Standard OpenAPI-published envelope properties such as `custom_fields` remain because they are API property names, not tenant field metadata.

Field identity is `(source YAML filename, schema/root identity, field path)`. Component schema identity is `component:<schema-name>` and remains file-local because names collide across files. Inline root identity includes source file, method, path, operation ID, usage location, status/media type or parameter location. Nested objects use dotted paths; arrays use `[]`; wildcard map values use `.*`; `@allOf[n]`, `@oneOf[n]`, `@anyOf[n]`, `@ref`, and related paths are structural records rather than invented API names.

Requiredness is evaluated only against the immediate containing schema's `required` array. An array item or composition marker is structural and therefore `n/a`. Usage is propagated transitively through local schema references: `request`, `response`, `both`, or `unreferenced`. `unreferenced` means no operation request/response/parameter in this snapshot reaches the component; it does not mean unsupported. Runtime organization metadata/settings, plan, region, permissions, and configured providers remain authoritative. Updates are maintainer-triggered only; no repository generator or scheduler is added.

| Request-only roots | 3029 |
| Response-only roots | 2375 |
| Both request and response roots | 1214 |
| Unreferenced component roots | 580 |
| Flattened field/structure rows | 20987 |
| Unique field identities | 20987 |
| Duplicate field identities | 0 |
| API names duplicated across root/file scopes | 1023 |
| Unique unresolved reference records | 0 |
| Unique recursive-cycle records | 0 |
| Malformed source records | 0 |
| Zero-field roots | 3215 |
| REST request/response schema references or inline markers checked | 1084 |
| REST/OpenAPI schema reconciliation defects | 0 |

A flattened row is emitted for every published property and for structural nodes needed to preserve references, composition branches, array items, wildcard maps, and malformed nodes. Consequently, the row count intentionally exceeds the count of literal API property names. Exact duplicate API-name statistics count names that occur in more than one field identity; collision is expected and is why file/root scope is mandatory.

## Closure interpretation and TBDs

- Complete means every component schema plus every inline operation request, response, and parameter schema in these 42 files was inventoried and traversed with bounded cycle detection.
- Published references and compositions are preserved even when they contribute no literal property. Arrays, item targets, additional properties, nullable, enum, format, default, read-only, write-only, and descriptions are retained where supplied.
- Request/response usage is evidence from operation reachability only. A field reached only from a response is not treated as request-writable. A field reached from a request is not guaranteed to be accepted in every organization, plan, region, or operation beyond those listed.
- OpenAPI omissions remain unknown, not unsupported. Runtime organization metadata and settings override this static recognition layer.
- Published source omissions remain TBD and are never repaired through inference. The missing delivery-challan response shape is not a reconciliation defect and does not create a response root.
